item.title: Russia's exit from European anti-torture treaty takes effect, ending detention visits
item.description: The Council of Europe's anti-torture committee will no longer be able to inspect places of detention in Russia. Its president says independent monitoring inside the country has now ended.

item.title: Russia ordered back into ice hockey championships, several federations refuse
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled on 30 October that the International Ice Hockey Federation must readmit Russian teams, but Sweden, Finland and Latvia say they will not play. The IIHF board meets on Monday with Russia as its main topic.

item.title: Russia lost territory in Ukraine for a second month running, US research group finds
item.description: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy put the Russian toll in October at more than 54,000 killed or seriously wounded, the highest since the February 2022 invasion.

item.title: Poland to host Coalition of the Willing military exercise in November 2026
item.description: Nearly 5,000 soldiers will take part, a Polish radio station reports. The United States is not taking part.

item.title: Commission pauses national social media bans for children for 12 months
item.description: The freeze covers Austria's planned minimum age of 14, as well as draft laws in Greece and Denmark, until 28 July 2027. Vienna has called the move unacceptable.

item.title: EU funds drove a measured slice of Poland's growth, and the bill is now due
item.description: Poland's economy doubled since EU accession, but the government's own evaluation attributes only a modest share of that rise to EU money, while the deficit climbs. Both the gains and the costs now carry numbers as the next EU budget is negotiated.

item.title: Ukraine's drone strikes cut Russian refining to a record low, but repairs limit the gain
item.description: Ukraine's strikes have put more of Russia's refining capacity out of action than at any earlier point in the war, and measured quarterly output has fallen by more than a fifth. What the record does not settle is how long the damage lasts, because refineries have shown both quick repairs and lasting decline.

item.title: Attal proposes a joint primary of democratic parties to block Le Pen in 2027
item.description: Gabriel Attal made the call on TF1, but Bruno Retailleau rejected a primary involving Raphaël Glucksmann, warning it would serve Marine Le Pen.

item.title: Judges suspend Poland's Constitutional Tribunal president, police block Warsaw building
item.description: Judges from Poland's parliamentary majority suspended tribunal president Bogdan Swięczkowski and his deputy for one month on Friday, and riot police blocked access to the building. President Karol Nawrocki, who says the constitutional order was violated, abandoned a foreign trip and returned to Warsaw.

item.title: Shops looted and more than 100 police injured after riots in central Frankfurt
item.description: Police sealed parts of the city centre on Halloween night after a largely peaceful youth demonstration dissolved. Hesse's interior minister said most suspects arrested were aged 13 to 29.

item.title: European Commission consults on draft rules for AI Act enforcement cases
item.description: The proposal, open for comment until 9 November 2026, would let each investigative step reset the five-year penalty clock, up to a ten-year cap. The text is not yet Commission policy.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march in France and Germany over cost of living
item.description: Police in Berlin and Frankfurt reported injuries, arrests and looting after the protests turned violent, and France's interior minister called a molotov attack on a gendarme attempted murder.

item.title: French student unions call for school and university blockades next week
item.description: The call follows the police ban of a Paris demonstration route after five weeks of student and pupil protest. Minister Philippe Baptiste says there is a right to study but no right to blockade.

item.title: Russia veto leaves UN mission in Western Sahara without a mandate
item.description: The Security Council failed to renew MINURSO by 31 October after Russia blocked an American draft, and Moscow's own counter-draft fell short of the nine votes needed. France warned that an abrupt closure would be exceedingly alarming.

item.title: Ukrainian troops say Russia is preparing a major attack on Kherson
item.description: Soldiers report Grad launchers massed in forests east of the city and possible preparations to cross the Dnipro river. Kherson's deputy governor warns shelling could intensify from Monday.

item.title: Commission releases final €951 million to Czechia as it plans Frontex expansion
item.description: The payment, due in December 2026 once the Council confirms it, closes Czechia's recovery plan. The same week, a report by advisers led by Catherine Day set out the Commission's biggest shake-up in two decades.
